comment: Consumer verification vectors for Android runtime payload publication. Each case is a complete consumer input and the outcome the contract's ordered checks reach, with the stage that refuses it. A consumer must accept every accept case and refuse every reject case at its declared stage and for its declared reason.
test_keys_comment: Every seed here is public. A consumer registry must never contain any of these public keys, and a verifier should refuse them at registry load: a published seed accepted as a trust anchor is a forgery anyone with a clone of this repository can make.
canonical_form: UTF-8 JSON, keys sorted by code point, no insignificant whitespace, no escaping of characters that need none

cases.name: accept_verify_only_key_verifies_an_existing_payload
cases.note: A rotated key demoted to verify_only still verifies what it signed. A registry that admitted only active keys would make every earlier payload unverifiable at rotation.

cases.name: accept_unstripped_payload
cases.note: Strip state is recorded, not required. An unstripped payload is still a payload.

cases.name: envelope_duplicate_key
cases.note: A repeated key makes two documents of one. A parser that keeps either is choosing which to verify, so the text is not a document this contract defines.

cases.name: envelope_unknown_field
cases.note: A field the contract does not define is outside what a verifier knows how to judge.

cases.name: envelope_missing_artifact
cases.note: Every one of the nine fields is required, so an envelope without `artifact` is refused before anything it does carry is used.

cases.name: envelope_missing_signature
cases.note: An envelope that carries no signature is not a signed envelope with a bad signature; it is not a signature envelope at all.

cases.name: envelope_malformed_signature_63_bytes
cases.note: The signature decodes to 63 bytes. Length is grammar, checked before any key is consulted.

cases.name: envelope_malformed_signature_unpadded_base64
cases.note: Standard padded Base64 is required. An unpadded spelling of the same bytes is a second encoding of one signature, and the contract admits one.

cases.name: envelope_malformed_signature_noncanonical_base64
cases.note: The signature's final data character has a padding bit set. A strict decoder accepts it and yields the same 64 bytes, so the signature would verify; it is refused because the contract admits one spelling of a signature and this is a second.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_path_separator
cases.note: `artifact` is attacker-influenced until the signature is checked, so it must be a plain filename before anything could join it to a path. This one is validly signed; the refusal is about its form, not its authenticity.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_dotdot
cases.note: `artifact` is attacker-influenced until the signature is checked, so it must be a plain filename before anything could join it to a path. This one is validly signed; the refusal is about its form, not its authenticity.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_dot
cases.note: `artifact` is attacker-influenced until the signature is checked, so it must be a plain filename before anything could join it to a path. This one is validly signed; the refusal is about its form, not its authenticity.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_backslash
cases.note: `artifact` is attacker-influenced until the signature is checked, so it must be a plain filename before anything could join it to a path. This one is validly signed; the refusal is about its form, not its authenticity.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_control_character
cases.note: `artifact` is attacker-influenced until the signature is checked, so it must be a plain filename before anything could join it to a path. This one is validly signed; the refusal is about its form, not its authenticity.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_delete_character
cases.note: `artifact` is validly signed and not of its form: DEL is a control character. Keeping every string ASCII with nothing to escape is what makes the canonical bytes identical in every language.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_non_ascii
cases.note: `artifact` is validly signed and not of its form: the form is printable ASCII. Keeping every string ASCII with nothing to escape is what makes the canonical bytes identical in every language.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_quote
cases.note: `artifact` is validly signed and not of its form: a quote would need escaping in the canonical bytes. Keeping every string ASCII with nothing to escape is what makes the canonical bytes identical in every language.

cases.name: envelope_malformed_runtime_version_build_metadata
cases.note: `runtime_version` is validly signed and outside its form (build metadata).

cases.name: envelope_malformed_target_api_zero
cases.note: `target` is validly signed and outside its form (api zero).

cases.name: envelope_malformed_target_api_leading_zero
cases.note: `target` is validly signed and outside its form (api leading zero).

cases.name: envelope_malformed_artifact_size_above_2_to_the_53_minus_1
cases.note: `artifact_size` is validly signed and outside its form (above 2 to the 53 minus 1).

cases.name: envelope_artifact_size_too_long_to_convert
cases.note: A 5000-digit integer. Several parsers raise converting it rather than refusing it, and a verifier that crashes has not refused.

cases.name: envelope_artifact_size_with_exponent
cases.note: The right number spelled with an exponent. The form is decimal digits.

cases.name: envelope_deeply_nested_value
cases.note: A field whose value is an array nested thirty thousand deep, inside the size bound. No field is an array, and a recursive parser exhausts its stack before it can say so.

cases.name: envelope_lone_surrogate_escape
cases.note: `artifact` begins with the escape of a lone surrogate, which is not a Unicode scalar value and cannot be encoded as UTF-8. A verifier that admits it to canonical encoding crashes there.

cases.name: envelope_longer_than_64_kib
cases.note: A genuine envelope padded with whitespace past 64 KiB. It is refused unread, so the size of what a verifier parses is bounded before parsing.

cases.name: signature_does_not_verify
cases.note: Signed over different bytes: the size was changed after signing.

cases.name: signature_under_the_release_bundle_domain
cases.note: The same key, the same fields, signed under the release-bundle domain separator. The domain is what stops a bundle signature verifying as a payload signature.

cases.name: signature_by_a_key_not_in_the_registry
cases.note: The envelope names a key the registry does not hold. An envelope names a key; it cannot supply one.

cases.name: signature_by_a_revoked_key
cases.note: Revoked keys fail closed, including for payloads signed before revocation.

cases.name: signature_by_a_release_bundle_purpose_entry_with_the_same_key
cases.note: The signature verifies under the key material, and the entry's purpose is runtime_release_bundle. Purpose is an authorisation statement, never inferred from the key bytes. A conforming registry load refuses this entry; verification refuses it again on its own.

cases.name: signature_by_the_wrong_registered_key
cases.note: The envelope names the active key and was signed by the rogue key.

cases.name: identity_runtime_version_not_selected
cases.note: A genuine, validly signed payload from a different release. The consumer selected 2.6.0.

cases.name: identity_target_not_a_v2_target
cases.note: Well-formed and validly signed, naming a target this contract does not list. A consumer refuses a target it does not know rather than guessing.

cases.name: identity_slot_is_not_a_v2_target
cases.note: The consumer's own slot is a target this contract does not list, and the envelope names that same target. Target and slot agree, so only the v2 membership check refuses it.

cases.name: identity_android-arm64-v8a-api21_payload_in_android-armeabi-v7a-api21_slot
cases.note: A correctly built payload with a valid signature for its own target, exported into another slot. Every property of the file is genuine, which is why only the identity check catches it.

cases.name: identity_android-arm64-v8a-api21_payload_in_android-x86_64-api21_slot
cases.note: A correctly built payload with a valid signature for its own target, exported into another slot. Every property of the file is genuine, which is why only the identity check catches it.

cases.note: A correctly built payload with a valid signature for its own target, exported into another slot. Every property of the file is genuine, which is why only the identity check catches it.

cases.note: A correctly built payload with a valid signature for its own target, exported into another slot. Every property of the file is genuine, which is why only the identity check catches it.

cases.name: artifact_name_disagrees_with_derived_name
cases.note: A plain filename, validly signed, that is not the name derived from the selected version and slot. Comparing it with the downloaded name would not catch this if both were renamed.

cases.name: payload_absent
cases.note: The envelope is genuine and the payload is missing. A consumer never substitutes a placeholder, a stub or a previously staged file.

cases.name: presence_before_basename
cases.note: The payload is missing and the name it would have been fetched under is wrong. Presence is step 5 and the basename step 6, so absence is what refuses it.

cases.name: downloaded_basename_disagrees_with_derived_name
cases.note: The envelope names the derived name and the file on disk was fetched under another. The signature says nothing about which file the consumer is holding.

cases.name: integrity_digest_mismatch
cases.note: Same length, one byte altered after signing.

cases.name: integrity_size_mismatch
cases.note: One byte appended after signing. The digest also differs; size is checked so a verifier that compared only digests prefixes would still refuse it.

cases.name: integrity_declared_size_wrong_digest_right
cases.note: The producer recorded the right digest and the wrong size, and signed both. The bytes are untouched, so a verifier comparing only the digest accepts an envelope whose own size claim is false.

cases.name: abi_android-armeabi-v7a-api21_bytes_signed_as_android-arm64-v8a-api21
cases.note: A producer that mislabelled: the envelope, the name, the digest and the slot all agree, and the ELF header describes a different ABI. The signature proves only that these bytes were signed.

cases.name: abi_android-x86_64-api21_bytes_signed_as_android-arm64-v8a-api21
cases.note: A producer that mislabelled: the envelope, the name, the digest and the slot all agree, and the ELF header describes a different ABI. The signature proves only that these bytes were signed.

cases.name: abi_android-arm64-v8a-api21_bytes_signed_as_android-armeabi-v7a-api21
cases.note: A producer that mislabelled: the envelope, the name, the digest and the slot all agree, and the ELF header describes a different ABI. The signature proves only that these bytes were signed.

cases.note: A producer that mislabelled: the envelope, the name, the digest and the slot all agree, and the ELF header describes a different ABI. The signature proves only that these bytes were signed.

cases.note: A producer that mislabelled: the envelope, the name, the digest and the slot all agree, and the ELF header describes a different ABI. The signature proves only that these bytes were signed.

cases.note: A producer that mislabelled: the envelope, the name, the digest and the slot all agree, and the ELF header describes a different ABI. The signature proves only that these bytes were signed.

cases.name: abi_width_only_aarch64_machine_at_32_bit_class
cases.note: The machine matches the slot and the class does not. A check that read only e_machine accepts it.

cases.name: abi_width_only_arm_machine_at_64_bit_class
cases.note: The machine matches the slot and the class does not. A check that read only e_machine accepts it.

cases.name: abi_big_endian
cases.note: Every Android ABI here is little-endian.

cases.name: abi_not_an_elf
cases.note: No ELF magic at all.

cases.name: abi_shorter_than_an_elf_header_prefix
cases.note: The ELF magic and identification bytes, and nothing where e_machine would be. A verifier must refuse it rather than index past the end.

cases.name: abi_first_magic_byte_wrong
cases.note: Every header byte right except the first byte of the magic.

cases.name: abi_before_content
cases.note: An armeabi-v7a header, signed as arm64, carrying a shell interpreter line. The ABI is step 8 and content step 9, so the ABI is what refuses it.

cases.name: content_shell_interpreter_line
cases.note: A valid arm64 header carrying a shell interpreter line. The consuming application ships a shell script to keep its own build green, and a payload containing one is that script.

cases.name: content_placeholder_marker
cases.note: A valid arm64 header carrying the placeholder marker.
